Write A, B, C for the angles of triangle ABC and R = OA = OB = OC for its circumradius.

Plan: it suffices to show that AH = 2R·cos A and MaO = R·cos A.

1. The altitudes of △ABC meet at H, so CH ⟂ AB. (1)

2. OB = OC and MaB = MaC, so OMa is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence OMa ⟂ BC. (2)

3. We show that AC = 2R·sin B:

AC = AB·sin B / sin C    [law of sines in △ABC]
   = 2·AB·sin B·cos C / sin∠BOA    [sin∠BOA = 2·sin C·cos C (central angle ∠AOB = 2∠ACB)]
   = 2·AB·sin B·sin∠OAB / sin∠BOA    [cos C = sin∠OAB (central angle ∠AOB = 2∠ACB; OA = OB: triangle OAB is isosceles)]
   = 2·AB·sin B·sin∠OBA / sin∠BOA    [law of sines in △ABO; OA = OB]
   = 2R·sin B    [law of sines in △ABO] (3)

4. We show that BH = 2R·sin∠HCB:

BH = BC·sin∠HCB / sin∠CHB    [law of sines in △BCH]
   = BC·sin∠HCB / sin A    [sin A = sin∠CHB (BH ⟂ AC; CH ⟂ AB, by (1))]
   = AC·sin∠HCB / sin B    [law of sines in △ABC]
   = 2R·sin∠HCB    [by (3)] (4)

5. We show that AH = 2R·cos A:

AH = BH·sin∠HBA / sin∠HAB    [law of sines in △ABH]
   = BH·cos A / sin∠HAB    [cos A = sin∠ABH (BH ⟂ AC)]
   = 2·BH·cos A·cos∠HAB / sin∠COA    [sin∠COA = 2·sin∠BAH·cos∠BAH (AH ⟂ BC; central angle ∠AOC = 2∠ABC)]
   = 2·BH·cos A·sin B / sin∠COA    [cos∠BAH = sin B (AH ⟂ BC)]
   = AC·BH·cos A / (R·sin∠COA)    [by (3)]
   = BH·cos A / sin∠OCA    [law of sines in △ACO]
   = BH·cos A / sin∠HCB    [sin∠ACO = sin∠BCH (OA = OC: triangle OAC is isosceles; central angle ∠AOC = 2∠ABC; CH ⟂ AB, by (1))]
   = 2R·cos A    [by (4)] (5)

6. We show that BC = 2R·sin A:

BC = AC·sin A / sin B    [law of sines in △ABC]
   = 2R·sin A    [by (3)] (6)

7. We show that MaO = R·cos A:

MaO = BMa·sin∠MaBO / sin∠MaOB    [law of sines in △BOMa]
    = R·sin∠MaBO / sin∠OMaB    [law of sines in △BOMa]
    = R·sin∠MaBO    [∠OMaB = 90° (OMa ⟂ BC, by (2))]
    = R·sin∠OCB    [sin∠BCO = sin∠MaBO (OB = OC: triangle OBC is isosceles); OA = OB]
    = R²·sin∠COB / BC    [law of sines in △BCO; OA = OB]
    = R·sin∠COB / (2·sin A)    [by (6)]
    = R·cos A    [sin∠COB = 2·sin A·cos A (central angle ∠BOC = 2∠BAC)] (7)

8. AH = 2R·cos A, by (5) and MaO = R·cos A, by (7), so AH : MaO = 2, as required. ∎
